Kitchen Remodeling in Andover, KS

Andover grew fast in the 1990s and 2000s — and most of those kitchens are now showing it. The builder-grade cabinets, laminate countertops, and closed-off layouts that were standard in Andover's suburban growth wave weren't designed to last 25–30 years in a Kansas kitchen. They were designed to hit a price point. Particle-board cabinet boxes swell at the toe kick from mopping and dishwasher steam. Silicone caulk at the backsplash seam fails and lets moisture into the substrate. The range hood vent moves air but not smell. The layout was designed for a magazine photo, not for how a family actually cooks.

Wheatland Construction remodels kitchens in Andover and Butler County. We're a Veterans Approved Builder (ID: 00899), Home Advisor Certified since 2019, and family-owned since 2018. We pull permits, use our own crews, and build kitchens that hold up to real use — including Kansas winters and the humidity swings that come with living near the Whitewater River drainage east of town.

What Drives Kitchen Remodels in Andover

Andover's housing stock is concentrated in a specific vintage: 1990s through 2010s production builds in subdivisions east of K-96 - Monarch Landing, the neighborhoods along US-54 near Andover Sports Complex, developments off Andover Road near the high school. Many are in the Butler County unincorporated areas around Andover city limits. These homes share a few common kitchen problems:

Closed-off layouts. The 1990s builder-standard was a kitchen separated from the living areas by a wall or a half-wall with a pass-through. Open-concept has been the dominant preference for 15+ years. Removing that wall — if it's non-structural — transforms how the first floor functions.

Particle-board and MDF construction. Builder-grade cabinet boxes from that era weren't solid wood — they were particle-board or MDF wrapped in thermofoil or laminate. Thermofoil peels. MDF swells with moisture. By year 20, these look and feel like what they are.

Countertop failures. Original laminate countertops in 1990s Andover homes are typically at the end of their usable life. Seams at the sink have failed, edges are chipped, and the surface texture is worn to bare substrate in high-use areas.

Ventilation inadequacy. Most builder-spec range hoods recirculate air rather than vent outside, or they vent through a duct that was never properly sealed. This is a moisture and air quality issue, not just a smell issue. Kansas kitchens need proper ventilation.

We identify all of this during the free in-home consultation before we give you a scope or a price.

What We Build in Andover Kitchens

The most common Andover kitchen remodel scope includes:

  • Cabinet replacement or refacing — full replacement with plywood-box construction in frameless or face-frame; refacing as a cost option when layout and box condition are sound
  • Countertop replacement — quartz is the dominant choice in Andover right now for durability and maintenance; granite and butcher block in appropriate applications
  • Open-concept conversion — wall removal with structural assessment; LVL beam installation if required; permit through City of Andover or Butler County
  • Appliance upgrades — range hood with proper exterior venting, dishwasher and range replacement coordinated with cabinet and countertop scope
  • Flooring replacement — LVP is the common choice for kitchen and adjacent living areas in open-concept conversions
  • Lighting upgrades — recessed LED, under-cabinet lighting, pendant fixtures over islands

Our Process in Andover

Free consultation, honest scope documentation, permit through the City of Andover Building Department or Butler County depending on location, our own crews for demo and installation. We assess structure, plumbing, and electrical before we give you a final number. No surprises after demo starts.

Most Andover kitchen remodels run 6–10 weeks from permit issuance to final walkthrough.

Frequently Asked Questions About Kitchen Remodeling in Andover

How much does kitchen remodeling cost in Andover, KS?

Andover kitchen remodels range from $22,000 for a mid-range refresh (new cabinets, countertops, fixtures, lighting) to $75,000+ for a full gut renovation with structural changes and high-end finishes. The open-concept conversions that are popular in Andover's 1990s housing stock typically run $35,000–$55,000 for a kitchen and adjacent wall removal with proper structural work and coordinated flooring. We provide detailed written estimates.

Do I need permits for kitchen remodeling in Andover?

Plumbing, electrical, and structural work (including wall removal) requires permits through the City of Andover Building Inspection Division or Butler County for unincorporated properties. We handle all permitting. Unpermitted structural work is a material disclosure issue at resale.

How long does a kitchen renovation take in Andover?

6–10 weeks for most Andover projects from permit issuance to final walkthrough. Projects with structural changes or custom cabinet lead times may run 10–14 weeks. We build realistic schedules.

Can I remove the wall between my Andover kitchen and living room?

Often yes, but it requires structural assessment before commitment. We determine whether the wall is load-bearing, evaluate the beam span required if it is, and quote the structural work as part of the total scope. Most 1990s Andover production homes have identifiable structural patterns — we've seen enough of them to give you a reliable read early in the process.

What kitchen styles are most popular in Andover right now?

Transitional — clean lines, two-tone cabinet colors (white uppers, darker lowers or island), quartz countertops, under-cabinet lighting, and large-format tile backsplashes. Full Shaker farmhouse is also popular in the more rural Butler County areas east of Andover city limits. We execute any aesthetic direction — our job is the craft, not the style decision.

Do you handle plumbing and electrical as part of a kitchen remodel in Andover?

Yes — we coordinate licensed plumbing and electrical as part of our project scope. We don't hand you a list of subcontractors to call yourself. Kitchen remodels almost always involve both trades and we manage that coordination.
